title: AgentIdentityResolution
description: Agent identity resolution on POST /api/v1/sessions (TraigentSchema#616): the refusal bodies the Backend returns when it cannot resolve a request to exactly one agent, and the response shape of a read-only duplicate-agents report. No request field is added or constrained: the code locator travels in the existing open `metadata` object (`function_module`, `function_qualname`, `function_relative_path`, `function_name`) and is documented here, not typed. The canonical identity of an agent is the Backend-minted, project-scoped agent id; what a client declares (agent_key, agent_id, function_name) is a resolution input, never the identity. The resolved id is returned in the 201 body at `metadata.agent_id` (null for a JWT caller, who gets no session-agent binding); the top-level `agent_id` of the 201 schema is not populated by the Backend today. Resolution order, before any write: (1) the exact legacy lookup: the Backend derives one lookup value from `agent_key` (when non-blank) or else from `function_name`, and matches it first as an agent id and then as the project-scoped key or name. The request's own `agent_id` field is accepted but NOT used to select an agent. When an explicit `agent_key` was sent, that lookup is the whole resolution: a hit is returned and no code locator is compared (a differing locator never blocks it), and a miss creates. When no `agent_key` was sent, a name hit is reused, EXCEPT that when both the request and that agent carry a code locator and the two differ (module or qualname), the name hit is not reused: if no agent matches the request's own locator the result is `agent_identity_conflict` (nothing created). (2) Only when no `agent_key` was sent and step 1 found nothing (or found a name hit whose locator differs): the code locator, module from `metadata.function_module` plus the qualname from `metadata.function_qualname` (exact) or the flattened qualname recovered from `metadata.function_name` (not the top-level `function_name`). Exactly one match is reused, none creates a new agent, several is `agent_identity_ambiguous` (nothing created). `function_relative_path` is read as a hint and never compared, so a path-only move changes nothing. Whether renaming or moving a function yields a new agent therefore depends on the case: an unnamed function whose module or qualname changes gets a new agent unless an exact name hit or another agent with a matching locator is found; a named agent (`agent_key`) keeps its agent; a path-only move keeps its agent. Display names, objectives, knobs and the run or privacy mode are never identity. `agent_ref` is accepted by the request schema but RESERVED: the Backend does not yet use it. The content-less identity shape (server-issued `agent_ref` only, no customer-chosen label) is DEFERRED to a later slice with the SDK: today the Backend refuses every request that declares `content_less_v1` with 400 CAPABILITY_NOT_SUPPORTED before any write.

AgentIdentityAmbiguousResponse.description: 409 on POST /api/v1/sessions. More than one existing agent of the project matches the request's code locator. NOTHING was created (no agent, run, study or binding); retry with an explicit selector or after the duplicates are resolved. Fixed text; no request value is echoed. `details.candidate_agent_ids` is returned only to a caller authorized for every listed agent (API key: per-agent write access; JWT user: project editor plus the same per-agent check); any other caller receives the ordinary authorization denial, which carries no candidates.

message.const: More than one existing agent in this project matches this function. No agent was created; resolve the duplicates and retry.

error.const: More than one existing agent in this project matches this function. No agent was created; resolve the duplicates and retry.

candidate_agent_ids.description: Backend agent ids of the agents that match (existing ids, which may be caller-supplied legacy strings and are potentially customer content), in no order of preference (the Backend never picks a survivor).

AgentIdentityConflictResponse.description: 409 on POST /api/v1/sessions. The request's name (legacy `function_name` identity) matches an existing agent whose stored code locator is a DIFFERENT function, and no agent matches the request's own locator. The name match is never reused and nothing was created. Fixed text; no request value is echoed. `details.conflicting_agent_id` is returned only to a caller authorized for that agent (same rule as the ambiguous refusal).

message.const: An existing agent already uses this identity for a different function. No agent was created.

error.const: An existing agent already uses this identity for a different function. No agent was created.

CapabilityNotSupportedResponse.description: 400 on POST /api/v1/sessions. The request declares a capability this server does not support (raised for every request that declares `content_less_v1`, which the server does not yet answer in the create response; any other capability value is a schema violation, not this refusal). Raised BEFORE any write, so a client fails closed without leaving an agent, run or study behind. Fixed text; the offending value is never echoed and no `details` member is sent. A client that wants to fail even earlier can omit the capability and read the server's advertised `capabilities` from a previous create response.

message.const: A requested capability is not supported by this server; no session was created

error.const: A requested capability is not supported by this server; no session was created

AgentId.description: Backend agent id (agents.id): the same definition (type and content class) the create response uses for the `agent_id` it returns, (string or null in that schema; the Backend never sends null in a refusal). Minted as a UUID4, but an agent created through a legacy route may carry a caller-supplied id, so no stricter shape is claimed. Because such an id can be customer content, disclosing it in a refusal is a Backend decision (see the Backend follow-ups on TraigentSchema#616).

DuplicateAgentCandidatesReport.description: Response of the read-only 'possible duplicate agents' report for one project. NOT YET SERVED: the Backend implements the report as a service function only and exposes no route, so no path in optimization_endpoints.json references this shape yet. It lists candidate groups and never merges, relinks, reparents, rewrites a key or picks a survivor. Names, keys and descriptions are customer content and are never returned: only the Backend's existing agent ids (which may be caller-supplied legacy strings and are potentially customer content), timestamps and counts. The report applies no caps on agents examined, groups, candidates or run counts.

project_id.description: Id of the project the report covers, echoed unchanged from the caller's scope: a UUID, the default project's `project_<32 hex>` id, or another legacy id (the Backend column is String(128)). Restricted to base64url characters (which UUIDs, `project_<hex>` and ids such as `proj_other` satisfy); a legacy id outside that alphabet is not representable. Treat as potentially customer content.

enum: The relative file path is a hint and is not compared.
Residual race window: when no agent existed at check time, creation re-resolves under a PostgreSQL advisory lock; on SQLite there is no lock.

DuplicateAgentGroup.description: One group of agents that may be the same logical agent. `same_module_and_qualname` groups carry `locator_precision` (`exact`: every member has an exact qualname; `flattened`: none has; `mixed`: exact members plus flattened-only members that would resolve to them) and `uncertainty` low for exact, medium otherwise. `shared_hash_suffix_only` groups (older rows with no stored locator that share the `(hash)` suffix of their display name) carry no `locator_precision` and `uncertainty` high: a lead, never a match. `decisive` is always false: whether the members are one agent is the owner's call.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 string from a timezone-naive database column serialized with isoformat(), so it may lack a timezone offset; null when unknown.

run_count.description: Number of experiments (runs) filed under this agent, in the same tenant, project and owner scope as the report.
